answer: With a Hardware security key bound by DNS record proof with one identity per channel, the account is only as strong as its binding: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the DNS record proof is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. The record keeps every ripple visible, so anyone can audit the binding roll. When the spiral settles over the cipher, the binding holds because every channel answered its own challenge.
